  1. Windows 11 is collecting data on which coding agents and developer tools you use

    • Operating Systems
    • Privacy

    733 points · 624 comments · 16 Nov 2026, 22:58 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — The author reverse-engineered Windows 11’s MissionControlAggregator.dll and found telemetry categories for named coding-agent executables, desktop agents, and developer tools. Their testing showed a renamed cmd.exe run as codex.exe set the Codex cohort bit; the article says queued diagnostic data contains categories rather than prompts, source code, or duration-of-use data, and recommends disabling optional diagnostic data to prevent upload.

    Discussion — Commenters debated both the practical case for Linux or reduced reliance on Windows and the significance of the telemetry. Some viewed executable-category logging as unsurprising diagnostics and distinguished local logs from uploaded data; others objected that collection occurs locally before optional upload choices and that categorizing specific AI tools is more intrusive than generic logging.
